idiom_name: name-keyed lookup in a parsed tree (json-c json_object_object_get_ex / jansson json_object_get) with hand-written defaults
implementation_notes: C has no reflection, no runtime schema and no binding layer, so the classic reader structure has no substrate and must be written by hand: parse the payload into a generic tree and look up only the keys you need by name, treating "not found" as "use my default". Both json-c and jansson return the absence explicitly rather than failing - json_object_object_get_ex reports whether the key exists and yields the value, json_object_get returns NULL for a missing key - and because the reader never iterates the object, unknown producer fields are never visited and cannot break it. When the payload is a packed binary struct instead of a self-describing tree this tolerant route disappears; use an explicitly versioned envelope with a length/version prefix rather than reading memory positions.
pitfalls: json_object_object_get and friends return borrowed references, and json_object_new_* used for a default is a new reference: forgetting json_object_put() leaks, forgetting that a returned value is borrowed frees memory you still use.
"Absent" and "explicit JSON null" both reach the reader as a value: json_typeof(v) == json_type_null must be checked deliberately, otherwise a null becomes a zero default or vice versa.

Every nested hop must be checked for NULL: json_object_object_get_ex on a non-object returns 0, but calling json_object_get_string() on the result of a failed lookup in older APIs crashes or returns garbage.
